body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert — latency and 5xx spike on inference endpoints in az-1b. 200+ requests/s hitting 502/504s and median p99 latency jumped from 80ms -> 1.2s. source: metrics.alerts.edge_errors > threshold.

maya (oncall): on it. pulling up dashboards... can someone paste the error distribution?

network-eng: seeing increased tcp retransmits and ENI queue depth on a subset of hosts in az-1b. NLB health checks are flapping for ~30% of backend targets. packet loss looks localized to the host link.

maya (oncall): noted. is this an AZ-level fabric issue or isolated hosts?

network-eng: looks zonal — multiple hosts across different racks. traceroutes show asymmetry and elevated latency to the AZ1b gateway. also DNS resolver latencies are high for requests originating from that AZ.

jason (infra): AWS console shows ASG targets still running but we see kernel soft-errors on eni queues on a few g5 instances. opening support ticket with AWS now (case 1234567890).

ops-bot: Incident created: IN-2165432100. Severity: Sev2. Incident lead: maya (oncall). Post to #statuspage?

maya (oncall): yes — draft short customer note: "We're investigating increased latency and errors impacting inference in one AZ. Traffic is being shifted; no data loss." @ashley (cs) can you prep CS comms for top 10 customers?

ashley (cs): on it. pulling customer routing overrides and recent customer traffic spikes. will post a message to affected accounts and add Slack escalation for any paying customers hitting >5% error.

sre-lead: Mitigation options: (1) steer new inference traffic away from az-1b (prefer az-1a / eu1a) via routing policy; (2) increase cross-region pool capacity and enable immediate failover for reserved routes; (3) disable aggressive connection reuse from edge to problematic hosts. Recommend (1) + (2) now.

maya (oncall): executing routing change — adding az-1b to lower-priority pool and flipping routing policy to prefer az-1a. patch below:

maya (oncall): ```bash
# update runtime routing weights
redwood-cli routes set-weight --route inference-prod --zone az-1b --weight 0.2
redwood-cli routes set-weight --route inference-prod --zone az-1a --weight 0.7
```

ops-bot: Route update submitted, change id r-98765, will propagate in ~30s.

network-eng: also toggled resolver fallback: forcing clients to prefer regional resolver eu1 for DNS lookups originating from az-1b to avoid the high-latency VPC resolver path.

maya (oncall): quick healthcheck after routing change: error rate dropped to baseline for most endpoints, p99 latency improved to ~110ms but a few long-tail buckets still show 5xx from legacy sessions.

jason (infra): initiating rolling drain of flagged hosts in az-1b (10 hosts) and replacing with fresh instances. draining so existing sessions expire gracefully.

network-eng: AWS replied on support case: "We observed ENI transmit queue stalls tied to host Ethernet driver and are moving affected hardware. They recommended instance replacement and routing shift."

maya (oncall): good. marking degraded → mitigated for customer communication. keeping incident open for root cause and postmortem.

ashley (cs): sent initial customer note and opened 1:1 for customers with >3% error increase. no escalations so far.

sre-lead: next actions: collect packet captures, ENI metrics, kernel dmesg from replaced hosts, and correlate timeline with a recent kernel OS patch we rolled last week. postmortem owner: jason (infra). target timeline: draft RCA in 48h.

maya (oncall): thanks team — handing incident to oncall-adjunct (sre-lead) for extended follow-up. I'll remain available for questions. incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:
